text:
alex: Started a short Nsight timeline capture on an 8xA100 run for the kv-merge heavy workload. Seeing periodic stalls ~20-30ms every ~512 iterations. nvprof spikes point to NCCL all-reduce on ranks 0 and 3. attaching snippet below. :thinking:

maria: ugh that's in the hot path. can you paste the waterfall rows you saw? small-seq or long-seq config?

alex: short seq (seq=128), batch heuristic uses dynamic microbatching (auto batch size 8 -> 16). here's the sampled timeline excerpt from the capture:
```
[GPU0] compute 0.28ms | kvcache_read 0.02ms | ncclAllReduce 0.12ms (tail 1.05ms)
[GPU1] compute 0.30ms | kvcache_read 0.01ms | ncclAllReduce 0.10ms
[GPU2] compute 0.29ms | kvcache_read 0.02ms | ncclAllReduce 0.11ms
[GPU3] compute 0.27ms | kvcache_read 0.02ms | ncclAllReduce 1.20ms (outlier)
```

tj: interesting that one rank hit 1.2ms. could be tail due to async MPI progress or kernel scheduling. did you see any kernel selection fallback (fp16->int8 path) around the same time?

alex: no obvious kernel switches in the timeline, kernel selection logs show stable kernel_id=K128_F16 for attention. but we do see repeated small allreduces after KV merge steps. nvprof excerpt:
```
Time(%)  Time  Calls  Name
12.7%    1.2s  1024   ncclAllReduce
28.3%    2.7s  1024   attention_kernel
```

shreya: my hypothesis: small microbatches cause lots of tiny allreduces that don't overlap well with compute because our batching heuristic emits a flush after KV merge. If KV read/write has a synchronization point, that serializes network.

maria: +1. do we have custom timers around kv_merge and before/after allreduce? we need p50/p95 breakdown, not just nvprof aggregate.

perf-bot: benchmark job #108 finished — kv-merge baseline -> current branch: p95 latency +7.1%, tokens/sec p95 -12%. see /ci/perf/108

alex: I added coarse timers in runtime yesterday. current debug dump:
```
KVMerge::merge_loop    avg 0.45ms  sd 0.12ms
KVCache::read         avg 0.02ms  sd 0.01ms
AllReduce            p50 0.09ms p95 1.12ms p99 1.45ms
Compute (attn)       avg 0.30ms
```

dinesh: that p95 on AllReduce is concerning. could be NCCL progress on CPU side starving the GPU. try enabling NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for a capture to correlate async progress thread activity.

tj: also try running with fused_allreduce disabled (runtime flag --no-fused-allreduce) to see if the library fallback behaves better for tiny payloads. sometimes fused path has a higher tail for many small ops.

shreya: another angle — our batcher sometimes splits token groups across TP/PP boundaries creating more cross-rank comms. can we pin a test: single microbatch with larger prefetched KV so we avoid extra merges? if latency improves that implicates batching heuristic.

alex: plan: 1) run 3 short captures (nsight)
- baseline branch with fused_allreduce on (same config)
- branch with fused_allreduce off (--no-fused-allreduce)
- branch with kvcache-prefetch enabled (increase prefetch window)
I'll set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and perf counters on CPU to grab progress thread timestamps.

maria: please also capture small nvprof with sampling every 1ms to get fine-grained tail distribution. keep run length ~5k iters so file sizes stay reasonable. :eyes:

alex: will do. logging conventions for the dumps? name them with job id + tag, e.g., 108-allreduce-tail-ss128-nsight.collect

dinesh: I'll schedule a 1hr sweep on infra side to run the three configs across 8 nodes and collect perf-bot summaries. if we see consistent p95 regressions on fused path, we can revert kernel selection heuristics for small payloads.

tj: tiny extra suggestion — add a per-allreduce debug counter to record byte-counts and whether operation used in-place vs out-of-place buffer. that will help confirm if copying is incurring extra host traffic.

shreya: good call. also add a flame/heatmap metric for inter-GPU idle time per iteration to surface which stage is waiting.

alex: OK starting the first capture now. dropping initial artifacts in /tmp/nsight/108-run1 and will post links. thanks all. :party:
